chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Moving like gypsies and learning to make friends
summary: The family moved every one to two years, forcing Thompson to make friends, sometimes through fights, and perhaps pushing him toward travelling music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Sir Charles, what else in those years, those years after the age of 12, what else was significant that you remember in those days?

Well, I think one of the most important things that was significant during that time, other than the things I've discussed already, was the amount of time we used to move as a family, of a minister. We moved so often it was almost like living the life of a gypsy throughout my early childhood. We lived, oh, from a period of one to two years at the average at each place, and this always affected me as a young fellow because I always had to be picking up, moving to new neighborhoods and making new friends. As you asked me previously, did I make friends. Well, in moving so often you had to make friends. I had to learn how to make friends. Sometimes it came about by some very unfortunate incidents, you know, moving to a new neighborhood sometimes you have to get acquainted in a rather rough manner, you know.

Yes. In other words many times I had those boyhood fights, you know, with the new neighbors, because as I said, being rather small in stature, and playing the violin and those things, and being the son of a minister, many of the boys in the new neighborhoods would challenge me, you know, to see what I was made out of. Those sort of things, you know.

And of course it was rather tiring, and quite an experience not to be able to settle in a place and have friends that you made from a boyhood day up until manhood. And this had quite a bit to do, I think, with my entire thinking, and perhaps it could have had something to do with my decision finally to become a travelling musician.
Did that persist right up until the time you left home?
